translation: The jade hall (玉堂) is in the upper palate inside the mouth, also called the upper chamber (上含); its orifice is the nasopharynx (頏顙). If it is touched and stabbed and injured on the left or right, there is only swelling and pain; if the central hole is touched and injured, it connects upward to the bridge of the nose, and must injure the rolled flesh of the nostril (commonly called the nose whiskers, 鼻須), or if it again violates the empty orifice (commonly called the jade hall, 玉堂), then blood flows without stopping, so that the nose and eyes both swell, the whole face is blue-purple, the spirit is weary, the head is dizzy, the four limbs are without strength, and the pain reaches the brain and marrow; if the epiglottis (會厭) and the upper transverse bone are injured, mild cases heal easily, but severe cases cannot speak; if the pain reaches the heart and diaphragm, then there is coma and heaviness. Urgently apply nifen (膩粉) and borneol (冰片) on paper, stick it on the broken flesh to stop the blood; internally take Zheng Gu Zi Jin Dan (正骨紫金丹) to disperse stasis and settle pain, regulate qi and strengthen the spleen, calm the spirit and settle the will; then use crab yellow and dragon's blood (蟹黃血竭) decocted into a decoction, rinsing the mouth twenty to thirty times a day; if the qi is not harmonious and smooth and food and drink are taken in little, daily use persimmon frost (柿霜), jade dew frost (玉露霜), milk skin (牛奶皮), milk cake (奶餅), milk butter oil (奶酥油), and stir-fried millet flour (炒糜子面) and similar things, to cool and moisten and recuperate, and then it will heal.
